usual_baseline: Initial assessment is often fair, but reassessment is almost absent: 0% [1206] and 0.13% within 24 hours [1673]. Risk assessment for immobilised lower limbs was 32–45% [1358, 1228]. Operation notes lacked any VTE plan in 42% [1628]. Psychiatric wards did worst: 13% [3085], 0–8% [3152].
fix_that_works: An automated EPMA prompt raised 24-hour reassessment from 0.13% to 74% [1673]. A redesigned pathway with an electronic discharge block raised ED risk assessment from 32% to 93.1% [1358]. A teaching half-day and written policy raised discharge chemoprophylaxis from 57% to 98% [1628]. A discharge letter template reached 95% [1207]. A proforma on drug charts reached 100% [3085].
fix_that_fails: Teaching, posters and an EPR dropdown raised reassessment only to 3% within 24 hours [1206]. Teaching did not change prophylaxis after long arthroscopy (50% to 55%, p=1.0) [1699]. An aspirin policy reached 93% but symptomatic VTE stayed at 6.4% [1508]. Compliance dipped to 86% after rotation [1512].
consultant_advice: VTE assessment audits are very common. Initial assessment is usually fine because it is mandatory; target the gaps instead: reassessment at 24 hours, the plan in the operation note, and discharge prescriptions. Electronic prompts and templates beat teaching. Where possible, record VTE events, not just forms completed [1508].
